doc.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022

title: Mondello's work as trumpeter, writer and consultant
summary: He calls himself a freelance jazz trumpeter who also writes, consults and teaches; Rowe asks whether playing led to the rest.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Wow. Okay. I am, for lack of a better word, a free-lance trumpeter, primarily a jazz trumpeter who also is able and does a lot of work writing. And that extends into some other activities which sort of is a logical progression, sort of like the 2-5-1 of life. But that kind of moved into consulting, production consulting and creative consulting and other things, book consulting. It’s kind of like someone said to me one time, “What is it that you do?” So I says, “I’m kind of like Monty Rock III from the old ‘Tonight Show.’” “What do you do?” “I’m a celebrity.” That’s what he used to say. Either that or like the Banana Man you know, from Captain Kangaroo. But I do a lot of different things in the jazz world, and some things outside of the jazz world as well, and I have an awful lot of fun. In most cases it’s a labor of love and like I say, things seem to lead on and on and on. There’s always something. It’s sort of like you know those domino videos you see on YouTube you know. One leads to the next to the next, and it keeps me pretty busy and I really, really enjoy doing what I am doing. I teach as well online and in some cases in person, and clinics and just a little bit of everything. But right now I would say predominantly I’m working in my writing and consulting work.

Would you think, would all those dominoes have started and fallen into place if you hadn’t been a player first? And what I mean by that is sometimes I’m fascinated by people who are tremendous fans of the music or they make a living as perhaps a jazz journalists but they weren’t players first. So did your trumpet playing lead to all these things?
